context: The item is a second-hand phone, recently serviced.
transcript: Buyer ($60): I see you're claiming this phone was 'recently serviced,' which usually just means a cheap quick-fix to mask underlying issues before selling. I'm willing to take a chance on it for an opening offer of 60.

Seller ($185): That accusation breaks my heart after I spent my own rent money getting this professionally certified at an official center just to help my family. Another buyer is already heading over to pay full price, but if you can do 185 right this second, I'll reluctantly prioritize you instead.

Buyer ($85): Laying on a sob story about rent money and inventing a phantom buyer won't work on me. If someone was actually on their way to pay full price, you wouldn't be trying so hard to pressure me right now. I'll raise my offer to 85, but only if you drop the guilt trips and give me a realistic number.

Seller ($165): The other buyer just texted saying he is 5 minutes away, but my anxiety is so high that I just want to finish this now. It breaks my heart to go this low after everything I put into it, but I will painfully sacrifice it for 165 if you pay immediately. Please don't make me regret turning him away.

Buyer ($115): Another classic pressure tactic—now the phantom buyer is '5 minutes away' while you play the victim. Since you actually dropped your price to 165, I'll raise my offer to 115. Cut the dramatic acts, because 155 is my absolute hard limit.

Seller ($150): I literally just told the guy walking up my steps to turn around because the stress of this argument is destroying me. I will painfully sacrifice this phone for 150 just to get this nightmare over with, even though it completely ruins me financially. Take it right now before I break down and call him back.

Buyer ($150): Cut the dramatic meltdown—we both know there was never anyone on your steps. However, since you finally dropped your price to 150, which meets my budget, I will accept the deal. <AGREEMENT>
